name: net
description: TCP network socket operations. Provides functions for creating TCP servers, connecting to remote hosts, and sending/receiving data over sockets. Sockets are represented as integer file descriptors.  Example (client):   use net    "localhost" 8080 net::connect! -> sock   sock "Hello" net::send! -> _   sock 1024 net::receive! -> _ -> data   data print nl   sock net::close  Example (server):   use net    8080 net::listen! -> server   server net::accept! -> client   client 1024 net::receive! -> _ -> data   client data net::send! -> _   client net::close   server net::close

constants.name: ErrListen
constants.description: Listen/bind failed. Port may be in use or permission denied.

constants.name: ErrAccept
constants.description: Accept failed. Could not accept incoming connection.

constants.name: ErrConnect
constants.description: Connection failed. Host unreachable or connection refused.

constants.name: ErrSend
constants.description: Send failed. Could not send data over socket.

constants.name: ErrReceive
constants.description: Receive failed. Could not receive data from socket.

functions.name: listen
functions.description: Create a TCP server socket, bind to the specified port, and start listening for connections. Sets SO_REUSEADDR and uses a backlog of 128.
errors: ErrListen - Port may be in use or permission denied

functions.name: accept
functions.description: Accept an incoming connection on a server socket. Blocks until a client connects.

functions.name: connect
functions.description: Connect to a remote host. Resolves hostnames via DNS. Returns a connected socket descriptor.
errors: ErrConnect - Host unreachable or connection refused

functions.name: send
functions.description: Send data over a connected socket.

functions.name: receive
functions.description: Receive data from a connected socket. Reads up to max_bytes (maximum 1MB). Returns the received data as a string and the actual number of bytes read.

functions.name: shutdown
functions.description: Gracefully shut down a socket for writing (SHUT_WR). Use before close for clean TCP teardown.

functions.name: close
functions.description: Close a socket and release associated resources.
